title: Lakhpati Didi Yojana 2026: 3 Cr Women, Rs 5L Interest-Free Loan
meta_description: 3.01 Cr women already became Lakhpati Didis. New target: 6 Cr by 2029. Lakhpati Didi 2.0 offers Rs 5 lakh interest-free loans + SHE-Marts via SHGs.

hero.one_liner: Helps rural Self-Help Group (SHG) women earn over ₹1 lakh annual household income - already crossed 3 crore beneficiaries; new target 6 crore by March 2029

what_is_it: Lakhpati Didi Yojana is a Government of India initiative launched in 2023 under the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM). Its goal is to enable women members of rural Self-Help Groups (SHGs) to earn a sustainable annual household income of at least ₹1,00,000 (one lakh rupees).

A "Lakhpati Didi" is technically defined as a woman SHG member with a sustainable annual household income of ₹1 lakh or more, maintained for a minimum of four agricultural seasons or business cycles, with an average monthly income of at least ₹10,000.

The original target was 3 crore Lakhpati Didis by March 2027. This was achieved ahead of schedule - by early 2026, 3.01 crore women had crossed the ₹1 lakh threshold. In February 2026, the Union Rural Development Minister announced the new target: 6 crore Lakhpati Didis by 2029-30. The scheme works alongside the Lakhpati Didi 2.0 expansion announced in Union Budget 2026-27, which provides interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh and community-owned SHE-Marts for market access.

extra_sections.title: Lakhpati Didi 2.0 - announced in Budget 2026-27
extra_sections.content: The Finance Minister announced an expanded version in Union Budget 2026-27 with three major upgrades: (1) interest-free loans up to ₹5 lakh for individual SHG members through the LokOS App, (2) community-owned SHE-Marts for direct market access, and (3) Self-Help Entrepreneur (SHE) initiatives - moving women from credit-supported livelihoods to enterprise ownership. The overall Gender Budget was also raised 11% to over ₹5 lakh crore.

extra_sections.heading: What Does "Lakhpati Didi" Actually Mean?
content: The technical definition matters because it shapes who is counted and what counts as success. According to the Ministry of Rural Development:
A Lakhpati Didi is a woman member of a Self-Help Group (SHG) whose household earns ₹1,00,000 or more per year - sustainably.
Sustainable means the income must be maintained for at least four agricultural seasons or business cycles. A one-time good year does not qualify.
The average monthly income should be at least ₹10,000 across these cycles, from any combination of agriculture, livestock, micro-enterprise, services, or wage employment.

Important: This is household income, not just the woman's individual income. The programme treats the family economy as the unit, recognising that SHG members typically support their entire household through their earnings.

extra_sections.heading: Are You Eligible to Become a Lakhpati Didi?
qualify: You are a rural woman aged 18 or above
You are a member of an active SHG (or willing to join one)
Your SHG is registered under DAY-NRLM
You have regular savings record in your SHG
You have a Jan Dhan or regular bank account
You are willing to take training and start a livelihood activity
disqualify: You live in Delhi or Chandigarh (DAY-NRLM is not implemented there)
You are not a member of any SHG (must join first)
Your SHG has been deregistered or is inactive
You are unwilling to participate in training or livelihood activity
Your SHG does not have a savings or credit history

extra_sections.heading: How to Access the ₹5 Lakh Interest-Free Loan
content: Under Lakhpati Didi 2.0 (announced in Budget 2026-27), SHG women can access interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh for individual enterprise. The process is digital-first via the LokOS App:
Step 1: Ensure your SHG is active and registered on the DAY-NRLM portal. Your Bank Sakhi (a trained financial facilitator) will verify your individual savings and credit history.
Step 2: Meet your local Community Resource Person (CRP). They will create your digital profile in the Digital Aajeevika Register using the LokOS App.
Step 3: Present your micro-business idea - dairy unit, food catering, organic compost, tailoring, etc. The CRP uploads your plan for approval by Block officials.
Step 4: Once approved, the interest-free loan is disbursed to your bank account. A PM Jan Dhan Yojana account is recommended, as it offers additional overdraft facility.

extra_sections.title: Do not pay anyone to "register" you under Lakhpati Didi
extra_sections.content: There is no separate Lakhpati Didi registration form. You only need to be an active member of a DAY-NRLM SHG. If anyone asks for money - to register, to get a loan, or to make you a Lakhpati Didi - it is a scam. Approach your village's existing SHG, the Community Resource Person, or Bank Sakhi directly. All government services are free.

how_to_apply.title: Join or form a Self-Help Group (SHG)
how_to_apply.description: If your village already has an SHG under DAY-NRLM, join it. If not, form a new SHG with 10-20 women from your community. Approach your Block Mission Management Unit (BMMU) of NRLM for help with formation and registration.

how_to_apply.title: Build savings and credit record
how_to_apply.description: Your SHG must demonstrate at least 3-6 months of regular monthly savings to qualify for SHG-Bank linkage and government grants. Each member typically contributes ₹10-100 per month into the group savings.

how_to_apply.title: Get trained for a livelihood
how_to_apply.description: Through DAY-NRLM, you receive free skill training in your chosen livelihood - dairy, food processing, tailoring, agriculture, etc. Training is conducted at the Block / District level, often by RSETI (Rural Self Employment Training Institutes).

how_to_apply.title: Apply for loan and start livelihood
how_to_apply.description: After training, access interest-free loan (up to ₹5 lakh under Lakhpati Didi 2.0) via the LokOS App through your Community Resource Person. Start your livelihood, sustain it across 4 seasons / cycles, and you officially become a Lakhpati Didi.

faqs.question: Who is a Lakhpati Didi?
faqs.answer: A Lakhpati Didi is a rural woman member of a Self-Help Group (SHG) under DAY-NRLM whose household earns ₹1,00,000 or more per year, sustainably across at least four agricultural seasons or business cycles, with average monthly income of at least ₹10,000. The income can come from any combination of agriculture, livestock, micro-enterprise, services, or wage employment.

faqs.question: How many women have become Lakhpati Didis so far?
faqs.answer: As of early 2026, 3.01 crore women have become Lakhpati Didis - crossing the original target of 3 crore that was set for March 2027. The new target announced by the government is 6 crore Lakhpati Didis by 2029-30.

faqs.question: How can I become a Lakhpati Didi?
faqs.answer: You must be a member of an active Self-Help Group (SHG) registered under DAY-NRLM (the National Rural Livelihoods Mission). If your village does not have an SHG, you can form one with 10-20 women. After your SHG builds 3-6 months of savings history, you qualify for free skill training and an interest-free loan up to ₹5 lakh (under Lakhpati Didi 2.0) to start your micro-enterprise.

faqs.question: Is Lakhpati Didi a cash transfer scheme?
faqs.answer: No. Unlike Majhi Ladki Bahin or Mahtari Vandan, Lakhpati Didi does NOT pay ₹1 lakh in cash to women. The ₹1 lakh refers to the annual household income target that women should earn through their own livelihood activities. The government provides training, capital (interest-free loans up to ₹5 lakh), and market access to help women reach this income level.

faqs.question: What is Lakhpati Didi 2.0?
faqs.answer: Lakhpati Didi 2.0 is the expanded version announced in Union Budget 2026-27. It introduces three major upgrades: (1) interest-free loans of up to ₹5 lakh to individual SHG women via the LokOS App, (2) community-owned SHE-Marts (Self-Help Entrepreneur Marts) for direct market access, and (3) a shift from credit-supported livelihoods to full enterprise ownership for advanced participants.

faqs.question: Can urban women apply for Lakhpati Didi Yojana?
faqs.answer: Lakhpati Didi is part of DAY-NRLM (National Rural Livelihoods Mission), so it specifically targets rural women. The corresponding scheme for urban women is the Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Urban Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NULM), which has similar SHG-based programmes but a separate framework. Lakhpati Didi targets and milestones apply to rural SHG members only.

faqs.question: What kind of livelihoods can I start under Lakhpati Didi?
faqs.answer: Most successful Lakhpati Didis are in: dairy and livestock (cow, buffalo, goat), food processing (pickles, papad, masala), agriculture and allied activities (vegetable cultivation, mushroom, beekeeping), handicrafts and textiles (tailoring, weaving, embroidery), banking correspondent (Bank Sakhi) roles, and retail through SHE-Marts. Your local Community Resource Person can advise on what works best in your area based on local demand.

faqs.question: How long does it take to earn ₹1 lakh annually?
faqs.answer: There is no fixed timeline - it depends on your livelihood, capital, and effort. Successful Lakhpati Didis typically reach ₹1 lakh annual household income within 2-4 years of joining an SHG and starting a livelihood. The programme defines the milestone as sustainable income maintained for at least 4 agricultural seasons or business cycles (roughly 1-2 years of consistent earnings) to qualify as a Lakhpati Didi.
